items.action: Build after upgrading, and rename a member of yours the compiler reports as colliding.
items.appliesWhen: Only a class of yours that extends TooltipDirective. Template users of dsTooltip need nothing; subclassing a DS component is unsupported.
items.pitfall: A redeclared private member collides as a public one does, and override cannot resolve it (TS2415); only a rename does.
items.verify: The app builds with no TS2415 or TS4114 against TooltipDirective.

items.action: Open every tooltip whose text holds a line break; keep the break where it reads well, otherwise join the lines with a space before binding.
items.appliesWhen: A dsTooltip string, or the text a dsTooltipWhenClipped host discloses, that contains a newline. A text on one line is unchanged, and runs of spaces still collapse.
items.pitfall: A template literal written across several source lines now shows one row per source line; the build and a unit test both pass over it.
items.verify: Hover each tooltip whose text comes from data or from a multi-line literal and confirm its lines break where intended.

informational: TableColumn takes an optional hint: the ds-table header label gets a dotted underline and shows the hint in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus. A non-sortable label with a hint renders as a button styled like the label; a sortable one keeps its sort button as the only Tab stop. While the label is clipped the tooltip shows the label and then the hint; otherwise the hint alone.

informational.text: A ds-table header label wider than its column clips with an ellipsis inside the column instead of running over the next header; the sort icon and the filter button stay visible. A header that fits looks the same, but every label now sits in a .th-text span, which carries the ellipsis, inside .th-label.
informational.verify: set a narrow width on a sortable, a plain and a filterable column with a long label and confirm each label ends in an ellipsis inside its column, the sort icon and filter button stay visible, and no label overlaps the next header; confirm a header that fits looks as before, including any stylesheet of yours that targets the label.
